messages:
karen_sales: Heads up - Meridian Bank wants a Private POC next month. Requirements: PrivateLink for control plane, outbound flows must go through their corporate proxy (they do TLS interception), and security will only accept IP allowlists. They asked if we can offer a short list of stable egress IPs or support proxy-auth. Adding @diego_eng and @olivia_netops to scope network and pricing.

diego_eng: Quick summary: three options for Meridian:
1) PrivateLink (control plane) + NAT egress from our Dedicated stack with reserved EIPs (we provide EIP list). Least friction for TLS-inspect.
2) PrivateLink + their proxy with client auth. We don't support NTLM/Kerberos; Basic auth or token-based proxy headers possible but enterprise proxies vary.
3) VPC peering (if they can accept routing changes) but peering leaks routes and is heavier operationally.

olivia_netops: Firewall snippet for option 1 (customer outbound allowlist):
```
# Meridian outbound allowlist (example)
ALLOW TCP 443 TO 3.122.45.10,3.122.45.11  # control-plane EIPs (us-east-1)
ALLOW TCP 8443 TO 3.122.45.20               # runtime plane EIP (dedicated)
# DNS: allow outbound to their resolver or to 1.1.1.1 for FQDN resolution
```
We'll publish final EIPs per region in the SOW.

max_sre: A couple gotchas: if their proxy does TLS MITM they must trust our client certs for PrivateLink hostnames OR we must use NAT EIPs. Also some corporate proxies choke on gRPC over 8443; if that happens we can fall back to HTTP/1.1 chunked responses on 443 (slower). Need customer to confirm whether their proxy supports CONNECT and gRPC passthrough.

karen_sales: They said their proxy performs TLS re-sign and their DLP team insists on IP allowlist only. So they prefer EIPs. They also asked about customer-managed keys and whether we have FIPS builds.

diego_eng: CMKs: yes for Private deployments. FIPS: available for Dedicated stacks but requires an ops change and a slightly longer lead time.

olivia_netops: Pricing rough for a 14-day POC (pro-rated): one-time eng setup $1,300; Dedicated compute prorated ~$2,100; NAT + reserved EIPs prorated ~$320; estimate bandwidth 150GB -> $30. We can offer a 14-day POC bundle at $3,600 to keep approvals simple. Hosted would be cheaper but can't guarantee reserved egress IPs.

sec-bot: Reminder: attach SOC2 Type II summary, runbook, and KMS doc when you send SOW.

max_sre: Action items: 1) olivia to produce final EIP list + polished firewall snippet (ETA 24h). 2) diego to draft POC SOW with $3.6k bundle + Hosted delta (ETA 24h). 3) karen to upload Meridian's security questionnaire and expected tokens/day. Once we have expected TPS and token volume we can refine egress bandwidth estimate.

karen_sales: Thanks everyone. I'll ask Meridian if they can accept NAT EIPs (preferred) and push the questionnaire now. Will update when they reply. :thumbsup:
